content.user_title: Maintain Project Memory Across AI Sessions
content.value_statement: AI coding sessions lose context when work spans multiple days or agents. This skill structures Memory Bank files so Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can resume work with current project knowledge.
actual_capabilities: Defines six core Markdown files for project brief, product context, active context, system patterns, tech context, and progress.
Provides startup, during-work, and session-ending workflows for keeping project context current.
Includes templates for each Memory Bank file with sections for requirements, architecture, setup, decisions, and status.
Directs agents to create a memory-bank folder when one is missing.
Supports optional documentation for complex features, integrations, APIs, tests, and deployment notes.
limitations: It relies on the agent and user to keep files accurate.
It does not persist memory outside the project documentation files.
It does not validate documentation quality or resolve conflicting project notes.
It may add maintenance overhead for very small projects.

use_cases.title: Solo Developer Continuity
use_cases.description: Maintain requirements, decisions, and next steps between coding sessions without rebuilding context from chat history.

use_cases.title: Team Handoff Notes
use_cases.description: Create shared Markdown files that explain project state, setup, patterns, and remaining work for another contributor.

use_cases.title: AI Pair Programming Projects
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code a consistent project briefing before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Memory Bank
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a memory-bank folder for this project. Ask me for missing project goals, then draft the six core Memory Bank files.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Active Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Memory Bank files and update activeContext.md and progress.md with the work completed in this session.

prompt_templates.title: Document Architecture Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: After reviewing the codebase and Memory Bank, update systemPatterns.md and techContext.md with the current architecture, constraints, and setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Reconcile Project Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the Memory Bank against the current codebase. Identify stale assumptions, missing decisions, and progress updates before proposing edits.

output_examples.input: I am starting a new project and need persistent context.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for project goals, creates the Memory Bank structure, and drafts concise starting documents for future sessions.

output_examples.input: Update memory bank after adding authentication.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the completed authentication work, records active decisions, lists next steps, and updates known issues.

output_examples.input: A teammate needs to understand the system architecture.
output_examples.output: The assistant produces an architecture summary, setup notes, key patterns, and relevant decisions in the Memory Bank files.

best_practices: Review all core Memory Bank files before starting work on an existing project.
Update active context and progress after significant changes, decisions, or blockers.
Keep entries concise, dated when useful, and linked to real project behavior.
anti_patterns: Treating Memory Bank files as permanent truth after the code changes.
Saving secrets, tokens, or private credentials in project memory notes.
Creating long narrative files that make current state hard to scan.

faq.question: Does it store memory automatically?
faq.answer: No. It organizes Markdown files that an AI assistant can read and update during project work.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude Code and can guide Claude and Codex when they read the skill instructions.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It defines projectbrief.md, productContext.md, activeContext.md, systemPatterns.md, techContext.md, and progress.md.

faq.question: Can I add custom files?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill allows extra documentation for features, integrations, APIs, tests, and deployment.

faq.question: Should I include secrets?
faq.answer: No. Keep credentials, tokens, and private customer data out of Memory Bank files.

faq.question: When should I update it?
faq.answer: Update it after meaningful code changes, architecture decisions, clarified requirements, or session handoffs.
